summary.headline: Sugs Lloyd H1 FY27 revenue rose 73% to INR213.31 crore and PAT 69% to INR20.01 crore, with order book at INR1,067 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR134.91 crore, up 12% YoY and 72% QoQ, making H1 FY27 the strongest half in company history. H1 EBITDA was INR31 crore at a 14.5% margin, and PAT was INR20.01 crore, with EPS of INR8.62 against INR6.86. Q2 new orders totalled INR395 crore excluding GST, all from outside Bihar, which cut Bihar's share of the order book from about 82% to about 55%. Management kept the INR1,000 crore FY28 target and the 10% product revenue goal, while operating cash outflow and debt (about INR160 crore) remained the key watch items.

segments.name: Power T&D (incl. smart grid)
segments.commentary: About 80% of H1 FY27 revenue, driven by RDSS and distribution project execution. Flagship partner project (about INR542 crore pre-GST) is due for completion by March 2028, and the Odisha maintenance contract adds about INR60 crore a year for 3 years.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Balance of H1 revenue. Amritsar solar plant scheduled for completion by December 2026. Management says EPC is becoming more competitive and it is shifting toward capex-plus-RESCO models through Sugs Renewables.

segments.name: Engineering products (FPI)
segments.commentary: Company says it holds more than half the domestic fault passage indicator market. Compact FPI completed testing and first unit to be supplied within the quarter. Target of about 10% of total revenue by FY28, covering all products together.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: INR1,067 crore at 30 September 2026 (about 3.5x FY26 revenue), of which about INR929 crore is power T&D and the rest solar. About 9/10 is with government utilities, PSUs and centrally funded schemes.

guidance_outlook: FY28 revenue target of INR1,000 crore remains unchanged; management said it is on track.
FY27 revenue target of INR600 crore and 10% product revenue target for FY28 described as intact.
EBITDA margin expected to average about 15% for the full year, with quarterly variation within the 14-15% band.
Management expects to add about INR400-500 crore of orders this year and said it would get more than that; about INR900-1,000 crore expected from bids within 6-9 months.
Year-end FY27 debt expected at about INR230-240 crore (beginning FY28), rising to about INR300 crore by end of FY28 at a debt-to-equity ratio of about 1.2-1.3x.
Management expects working capital interest rates to fall as external credit ratings improve. Company expects to remain cash negative while growth stays around 70%.
capex_capacity: FPI manufacturing capacity utilisation is under 5-10%; management says FPI capacity is not a constraint.
Vacuum circuit breaker (VCB) billing expected in FY28; ring main unit (RMU) billing about 6 months after that. Management did not quantify volumes.
Backward integration under consideration for frequently bought items.

Bid pipeline: INR19,150 crore of tenders floated, INR6,600 crore selected for bidding, and INR1,260 crore at final evaluation (about INR800 crore power T&D, INR400 crore solar and storage, INR60 crore products).
BESS: about 20 MWh bid across EPC and RESCO models, funded by a mix of equity and debt.
Subsidiary Sugs Renewables to bid for and hold RESCO projects for recurring revenue.
demand_pricing: Bihar share of order book fell from about 82% (end-July) to about 55% now; company operates in 10-11 states, and new orders came from Punjab (RDSS, 15 months), Odisha (maintenance, 3 years) and Noida and Madhya Pradesh power utilities.
Strike-rate targets of 15-20% on qualified bids and 10-15% in new states.
Competition in FPI is mainly Siemens; VCB competitors include Siemens, ABB, Schneider; RMU has many players. Management cites customisation and new-model development as entry barriers.
Management said a transmission tender in Jammu and Kashmir where it was L1 was scrapped after a state policy change; it has since bid for Rajasthan and other transmission tenders.
Management expects growth in SCADA through project-specific joint ventures with software partners; technical collaboration talks are ongoing with completion targeted by H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Margins fell to 14.1% in Q2 from 15.3% in Q1; what is the outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly variation is due to the mix of high- and low-margin items in long-duration projects. It expects about 15% EBITDA margin for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Debt was about INR160 crore versus a guided FY27 peak of about INR130 crore. What is the peak and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR130 crore referred to fund-based debt only. Total debt will be kept at about 1.2-1.3x debt-to-equity, with year-end FY27 debt of about INR230-240 crore and about INR300 crore by end of FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is unlikely while growth stays around 70%, because growth consumes working capital. Cash positivity would need slower growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR190 crore receivables will be collected within 6 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full INR190 crore is expected within 6 months. About INR200 crore was collected in H1, and about INR50 crore has been collected since quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for further equity dilution, and will unsecured promoter loans be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans for further equity dilution now. Promoters may extend unsecured loans if required, depending on the situation.

qa_highlights.question: Haryana and UP tenders reportedly disqualified; was this a one-time issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no disqualification. In Haryana, a document (a revised bank certificate format) was submitted late, which led DHBVN to disqualify the bid.

risks_watch: Working capital: receivable days still about 150 and operating cash outflow continues; growth of about 70% keeps the company cash negative.
Debt rising toward INR230-240 crore by March 2027 and about INR300 crore by March 2028, with the debt-to-equity ratio held at about 1.3x.
Margin variation quarter to quarter (Q2 14.1% vs Q1 15.3%); FY27 margin guidance of about 15% depends on mix.
Order-to-target gap: about INR400-500 crore of new orders is needed in 5-6 months to support INR1,000 crore FY28 revenue, and bids of about INR6,600 crore are pending.
Transmission and BESS revenue from H2 FY27 is uncertain after the J&K tender was scrapped and new bids are in evaluation.
Promoter support: the recent credit rating mentions promoter equity and unsecured loans, and management gave conflicting signals on the plan.
Tender compliance: a document submission delay led to a Haryana disqualification.
Product revenue (FPI, VCB, RMU) remains early-stage, with the 10% target by FY28 not yet visible in numbers.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, order inflow and FY28 targets, but more cautious on cash flow and debt. Management was less precise when asked about the working capital, equity and unsecured loan plans, and on the Haryana/UP disqualification it corrected the record.
key_quotes: Q2 revenue was INR134.91 crores, up 12% on the same quarter last year and up 72% on the preceding quarter, which is the Q1.
We go into the second half with the largest order book in our history and a far wider geographic base than a year ago.
Capacity for FPI is not a constraint.
As long as this growth remains 70% or this thing, we will remain cash negative.

growth.why: Management holds the INR1,000 crore FY28 target and INR600 crore FY27 target (implying roughly 67% growth off FY26 base is not stated directly; FY27 target used as guide), backed by a INR1,067 crore order book (about 3.5x FY26 revenue) and INR395 crore of Q2 orders, but no new plant capacity is being added since FPI runs at under 5-10% utilisation; VCB/RMU volumes are unquantified and billing star

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides about 15% EBITDA margin for FY27 with quarterly variation in the 14-15% band (Q2 at 14.1%, Q1 at 15.3%), so the full-year average holds near 15% but depends on project mix rather than a clear upward trend.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FPI capacity is under 5-10% utilised and management says it is not a constraint, so no new plant is being added; VCB and RMU lines are planned for FY28 but volumes are not quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book of INR1,067 crore (about 3.5x FY26 revenue) and INR395 crore of Q2 orders back the INR600 crore FY27 target and INR1,000 crore FY28 target, with INR900-1,000 crore more expected from bids in 6-9 months.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 5% of capacity, so no pressure for a new capex announcement; backward integration is only under consideration and BESS is bid, not built.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the INR1,000 crore FY28 target and INR600 crore FY27 target without raising them, and Q2 revenue was up only 12% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Order book needs INR400-500 crore of new orders in 5-6 months to support FY28 target, transmission J&K tender was scrapped, and receivable days are still about 150 with operating cash outflow continuing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: VCB billing expected in FY28 (about Q4 FY27 onward) and RMU about 6 months later; compact FPI first unit is supplied within the current quarter, though volumes are unquantified and product revenue is early-stage.

rows.label: Cash negative while growth stays ~70%
rows.why: Management says operating cash stays negative while growth is around 70%, with H1 operating outflow of INR12 crore and receivable days down from about 179 to about 150; it expects about INR190 crore of receivables collected within 6 months.

rows.label: Debt rising to INR230-240 crore by FY27 end
rows.why: Guided year-end FY27 debt of INR230-240 crore and about INR300 crore by end FY28 at 1.2-1.3x debt-to-equity, so leverage rises rather than falls; interest cost guided to fall as credit ratings improve.

rows.label: Bid pipeline conversion
rows.why: INR1,260 crore at final evaluation and INR6,600 crore selected for bidding, with management expecting INR900-1,000 crore from bids in 6-9 months, but the J&K transmission tender was scrapped and Haryana bid was disqualified over late document submission.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, order inflow and FY28 targets, and cautious on cash flow, debt and margin variation; analysts pressed on the debt peak vs guidance, the cash outflow, receivables, promoter funding and the Haryana/UP disqualification.
